title: Week 1 Experimental Game Creation - no art
author: selfish_meme
selftext:
I built a prompt using Claude Opus, in the prompt I put a lot of the ideas, characters and story for my game, the gameplay I wanted, what the setting and style would be, economics, interactions, I got Claude to ask me a bunch of questions to fill out a 'build me a game' prompt containing everything I could think of.

Then I told Claude to build the game with no art in Unreal Engine (I already had Unreal and Visual Studio all setup from previous gamedev, which would be a big step for beginners). It built the game overnight. It finished, 9 levels, 7 missions, many more characters and speech, economy, screens to interact with the game, generated simple meshes for the game to drive using primitives and the simplest possible method.  
  
And it was terrible. lol.

But it was a whole game, and it had eveything I had wanted in the game and it was playable. I have spent a week tweaking the game, we built a play script to play the game, and slowly it made it further and further through the game, as we went, we were tweaking gameplay, balancing, adding and removing characters, building on the story and subplots, adding and deleting elements. I think about Wednesday (started Saturday), the soak got the first full playthrough. I saw a post on here and started adding profiles for the soak, they each played a bit differently, added achievements for the over achievers, settings for the control freaks, hand holding for the confused etc. Tried to give 'fun' a measure by how much each profile got to do the thing it liked.

At this stage of the game it is quite playable and I am starting on the looks and art. This video is of the first few screens of the game, as I am doing the UI. It is in no way finished, but I thought that going this way without the art might be something people are interested in. I love to tweak and I tried to resist doing much about the way it looks until the game play was fairly complete and somewhat balanced. I think in this way it helped me concentrate on doing some of the less satisfying work first. Now I am adding art to a game that already works, not trying to add gameplay while I am constantly tweaking visually. We will see if it's succesful. I have a steam dev account and will soon put up a playtest so people can follow along it's development if they want. I will post again when it is up.
